subject: Climate & Environment
title: Offshore Wind Farms
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Offshore Wind Farms.

hook.text: Wind blows stronger and steadier over the ocean than over land. That's a huge advantage.

buildup.text: Denmark built the first offshore wind farm in 1991 with just 11 turbines.

discovery.text: Offshore turbines now stand 260 meters tall — taller than most skyscrapers.

twist.text: Floating platforms let turbines sit in deep water where winds are even stronger.

climax.text: The UK generates more offshore wind power than any other country on Earth.

punchline.text: The best wind farms are the ones you can't see from shore.

quiz.question: Which country built the first offshore wind farm?

details.summary: Offshore wind farms place turbines in ocean waters where winds are stronger and more consistent than on land. Floating foundations now allow deployment in deep water far from shore. Offshore wind capacity is growing rapidly, with Europe and Asia leading installation.
details.whyItMatters: Offshore wind offers enormous untapped energy potential with minimal land-use conflict. It is expected to become one of the world's largest power sources this century.
takeaways: Ocean winds are stronger and steadier than winds over land
Floating platforms enable turbines in deep-water locations
Global offshore wind capacity is expanding rapidly

faq.question: How are offshore turbines installed in deep water?
faq.answer: Floating platforms anchored to the seabed with mooring lines allow turbines in water deeper than 60 meters, where fixed foundations are impractical. Technologies include spar buoys, semi-submersibles, and tension-leg platforms.

faq.question: What are the environmental impacts of offshore wind?
faq.answer: Concerns include noise during construction that disturbs marine mammals, bird and bat collisions, electromagnetic fields from subsea cables, and habitat alteration. Careful siting, seasonal restrictions, and monitoring help minimize these effects.
